performance.title: Performance
performance.description: Keep 20–30 CLI sessions responsive and stop one heavy build from dragging down the whole machine. Most switches only affect newly started sessions.
performance.buildParallelismEnabled: Inject build parallelism into new sessions
performance.buildParallelismEnabledHint: Sets CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, MAKEFLAGS, CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL, RAYON_NUM_THREADS, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE and a ripgrep config; keys already in the environment are left alone. New sessions only.
performance.buildJobsHint: Leave empty for auto: max(2, cores − 8), keeping headroom for the UI and other panes.
performance.rgThreadsHint: Leave empty for auto: max(2, build jobs ÷ 2).
performance.codexLightweightEnabledHint: Launches Codex with TUI animations and auto recap off (tui.animations / tui.auto_recap) to cut redraw cost with many sessions open.
performance.codexLowSpecModeHint: Caps concurrent sub-threads per session at 2 (agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session). Turn on when the machine is struggling.
performance.heavyGateEnabledHint: Off by default = pass-through. When on, cc-panes-ctl run --heavy queues for a slot so several panes don't compile at once.
performance.heavyGateSlotsHint: How many heavy commands may run at once. Leave empty for auto: max(1, cores ÷ 8).
performance.heavyGateTimeoutSecsHint: Commands waiting longer than this are released anyway and logged.
performance.heavyLedgerEnabledHint: Hooks and the sampler write CPU/memory-hungry commands into local SQLite; see them under "Costliest commands" in the resource manager. Command lines are redacted and pruned after 30 days.
performance.heavyLedgerClearUnavailable: Clearing the ledger is not supported by this version
performance.sessionCpuWeightHint: 1–9; 5 is neutral and leaves it unset. Lower yields more to the UI and other panes. A safety net for runaway work, not a ceiling for normal work. Applies to newly started sessions.
performance.wslQuotaEnabled: Run WSL sessions in a systemd scope with cgroup quotas
performance.wslQuotaEnabledHint: Only takes effect when the WSL distro has a systemd user manager; otherwise falls back to nice.
performance.wslCpuWeightHint: systemd CPUWeight (1–10000, default 20). Only matters under contention; idle cores still run flat out.
performance.wslMemoryHighPercentHint: Percentage of physical memory (0–90) above which the kernel starts reclaiming; default 0 = unset, same as 0.12.21. Builds that cross it slow down noticeably.
performance.parkedTerminalLimitHint: How many hidden panes keep an unparked terminal instance (2–12); the least recently viewed are parked first and replayed from the backend snapshot when shown again.
performance.parkDelaySecsHint: How long a pane stays hidden before parking (5–600 s). Progress and waiting-for-input badges keep updating.

setupGuide.title: Setup Guide
setupGuide.description: Revisit the golden five-minute path and track real progress through the core parallel workflow.

agentChat.title: Agent Chat
agentChat.description: Structured agent conversations (ACP engines and Codex).
agentChat.codexForceAcp: Always use ACP compatibility mode for Codex
agentChat.codexForceAcpDesc: New Codex chats use the codex-acp bridge instead of the native App Server. Off by default: Codex uses the App Server and falls back to ACP automatically when it can't start. Existing conversations keep the transport they started with.

experimental.title: Experimental
experimental.description: Unstable features are managed here and retain their choices when they graduate.
experimental.emptyDescription: This release has no experimental options that require manual activation.
experimental.notice: These features are still being polished and are off by default. Turning one on reveals its activity-bar entry and related pages; you can turn it off again at any time without losing generated data.
experimental.dramaStudioDesc: The Drama Studio activity-bar entry and the screenplay → storyboard → shots → footage pipeline, including batch restyle (uses the media studio's provider selection).
experimental.librarySpaceDesc: Activity bar “Library” entry: create an AI-maintained materials folder (default ~/CC-Panes-Library) and open a Claude Code assistant that collects, transcribes videos and organizes.

modules.title: Modules
modules.description: Manage module entries. Hidden modules remain available from the Command Palette.
modules.allowAiDialogLabel: Let AI request a popup panel
modules.placementHint: Moving a module only changes its entry. Hidden modules remain available from the Command Palette.

usageStats.description: Review token and character usage across workspaces.

theme.title: Theme
theme.styleDescription: Choose the color theme and interface shape separately. Any combination can be used, and changes apply immediately and save automatically.

system.title: System appearance

theme.colorDescription: Controls application backgrounds, text, accents, and status colors.
theme.shapeDescription: Adjusts corners, dividers, and surface treatment without changing the current color theme.
theme.shapeScopeNote: Interface shape does not change the color theme, terminal theme, fonts, text size, or pane layout.
theme.wallpaperHint: The effect is more visible with a wallpaper. Without one, surfaces continue to use the current theme background.
theme.blurFallback: Background blur is unavailable in this environment. Translucent surfaces remain enabled.

custom.title: Custom tweaks
custom.description: Fine-tune the accent color, corner radius, and panel lightness on top of the current color theme. Changes apply instantly and save automatically; shape and wallpaper settings are unaffected.

soft.name: Soft
soft.description: Keeps the current CC-Panes corner treatment and light borders, so the upgrade does not change the existing appearance.

slab.name: Slab
slab.description: Uses tighter corners and subtle top-and-bottom edge contrast to distinguish adjacent panels.

sharp.name: Sharp
sharp.description: Removes container rounding so tabs, sidebars, and panels align to the grid.

glass.name: Glass
glass.description: Uses translucent, blurred chrome for the title bar, sidebar, and overlays while keeping terminals and inputs solid.

panel.name: Panel
panel.description: Uses square corners and clearer dividers to define panes and tool regions.

carbon.name: Carbon
carbon.description: Adds a low-contrast geometric texture to translucent surfaces while keeping terminal content clear.

density.title: Interface density
density.description: Adjusts row height and spacing in sidebars, status bars, and forms. Applies immediately and saves automatically.

comfortable.name: Comfortable
comfortable.description: Default row height and spacing for everyday use.

compact.name: Compact
compact.description: Tighter rows and spacing to fit more content on screen.

webAccessDescription: Start the local Web app with the same CC-Panes data. LAN access requires account credentials.

webAccessSection.startupEnabledHint: When disabled, the desktop app will not start the Web service.
webAccessSection.autoOpen: Open the browser automatically after startup
webAccessSection.autoOpenHint: Useful when using the Web app as the default entry point.
webAccessSection.authEnabledHint: When enabled, the Web API and terminal WebSocket both require a login session.
webAccessSection.passwordPlaceholderConfigured: Leave blank and click Save to clear the password
webAccessSection.allowLanEnabledHint: The service will listen on 0.0.0.0 when enabled.
webAccessSection.allowLanRequiresAuthHint: Enable account login and set a password first.
webAccessSection.remoteReadOnlyHint: Non-local sources (including Tailscale Serve) can only view after login; terminal input and file changes are blocked. Local browsers are unaffected. Restart the Web service after saving.
webAccessSection.remoteAuthenticatedWrite: Allow authenticated remote sessions to write
webAccessSection.remoteAuthenticatedWriteHint: Exception to read-only mode: remote devices logged in with account credentials (such as phones) can enter terminal input and perform write operations. Confirm that the remote link is trusted (Tailscale is recommended). Restart the Web service after saving.
webAccessSection.remoteAuthenticatedWriteRequiresAuthHint: Enable account login and set a password first; this switch has no effect without a configured password.
webAccessSection.ipWhitelistHint: Leave blank to allow any LAN client; separate multiple entries with newlines or commas.

orchestrator.title: Orchestrator (MCP endpoint)
orchestrator.description: Built-in CC-Panes orchestrator (for CLI ccpanes MCP tools to connect back). Restart the app after changing.

auto.label: Automatic (recommended)
auto.hint: Defaults to local-only; WSL can access loopback on mirrored networking, while NAT-mode WSL opens all network interfaces.

loopback.label: Local only
loopback.hint: Always 127.0.0.1. WSL can still access it on mirrored networking; in NAT mode, the CLI inside WSL may not be able to connect back to MCP.

all.label: All interfaces
all.hint: Always 0.0.0.0 (visible on the LAN, protected by a random port and token).

rotate.title: Access token
rotate.description: CLI sessions and external MCP clients use it to reach the orchestrator. Rotate it if you suspect it leaked.
rotate.confirm:
Rotate the orchestrator access token?

• The old token stops working immediately. The new token is saved and kept across restarts.
• MCP clients in other apps configured with the old URL / token must switch to the new URL shown under "Use in other apps (MCP)".
• {{count}} terminal session(s) are running now (plus any open Agent Chats). They received the old token at launch (in their environment and MCP config, which can't be updated live): CC-Panes MCP tool calls and status reporting in those sessions will fail until you close and reopen their tabs. Sessions connected through the cc-panes-ctl MCP proxy switch to the new token automatically.
• Sessions opened afterwards use the new token.
rotate.confirmUnknown:
Rotate the orchestrator access token?

• The old token stops working immediately. The new token is saved and kept across restarts.
• External MCP clients configured with the old token must switch to the new URL.
• Running sessions (including Agent Chats) received the old token at launch and can't be updated live: their CC-Panes MCP tool calls and status reporting will fail until you close and reopen their tabs.
• Sessions opened afterwards use the new token.
rotate.done: Token rotated. New sessions will use the new token.

tailscale.title: Tailscale remote access (recommended)
tailscale.description: Securely access the Web app from your own devices through Tailscale Serve: no LAN exposure is needed and the service stays bound to localhost. Detection is read-only; tailscale serve runs only when you click Turn on / Turn off. CC-Panes never stores Tailscale credentials.
tailscale.cliNotFound: Tailscale CLI not detected. Install it and try again: https://tailscale.com/download
tailscale.notRunning: Tailscale is installed but not running{{state}}. Run
tailscale.tailnetHint: Run the command above in a terminal, then access this address from any device in your tailnet. We recommend enabling "Account password login" and "Remote read-only mode"; Tailscale access is treated as a remote source. To unpublish, run

serve.hint: tailscale serve only runs when you click: turning on forwards your tailnet's HTTPS 443 to the local Web server; turning off removes only that entry. Requires an access password.

errors.notInstalled: Tailscale CLI not found. Install Tailscale first: https://tailscale.com/download
errors.notRunning: Tailscale is not connected ({{state}}). Run tailscale up in a terminal to sign in.
errors.needsApproval: Serve isn't enabled on your tailnet yet and needs admin approval. Open this link in a browser to enable it, then try again: {{url}}
errors.needsApprovalNoUrl: Serve isn't enabled on your tailnet yet. Ask an admin to enable HTTPS / Serve in the Tailscale admin console, then try again.
errors.permissionDenied: Not allowed to change the Tailscale Serve config. On Linux, run sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER and try again. Details: {{detail}}
errors.passwordRequired: Access through Tailscale Serve counts as remote. Set an access password under Sign-in first.

webAccessSection.restartHint: Changes to the port, LAN access, or password policy take effect after restarting the Web service.

imBridgeDescription: Push session events to DingTalk / WeCom / Feishu group bots
imPushWhenFocused: Push even when window is focused
imPushWhenFocusedDesc: When off, events are pushed only while the window is unfocused. IM push is most useful when you are away, so keeping this on is recommended
imPlainStorageHint: Credentials are stored in plain text in the local config.toml (same as Provider API keys). Avoid filling them in on shared machines
imNoChannels: No channels yet. Add a DingTalk / WeCom / Feishu group bot webhook to receive event pushes.
imChannelSecretHint: Secret for DingTalk signing / Feishu signature verification; leave empty if not enabled
trayShowSessionStatus: Show session status in tray menu
trayShowSessionStatusDesc: Show a session status summary and the pending list in the tray menu
trayMaxPendingEntriesDesc: Maximum number of pending sessions listed in the tray menu (1-10)
trayTooltipSummary: Show status summary in tray tooltip
trayTooltipSummaryDesc: Show a session status summary when hovering over the tray icon
trayConfirmQuitDesc: Ask for confirmation before quitting while sessions are still running
trayQuitConfirmDesc: {{count}} session(s) are still running. Are you sure you want to quit?
updateNotifyEnabledDesc: Show an update card in the bottom-right when idle. The status bar entry remains available.
featureTipsEnabledDesc: Occasionally introduce unused capabilities at natural idle moments.
localHistoryEnabledDesc: Turning this off stops file watching for every project. Project settings cannot override it; new sessions resume watching on demand after re-enabling.
dataDirDesc: Storage location for database, Provider config, and workspaces
memoryDbPathDesc: Leave empty to use memory.db in the data directory. Dev and release builds keep separate data directories; point both here at one file to share a single memory store.
migrationDone: Migration complete, please restart to apply
dataDirResetDone: Data directory reset to default, please restart to apply
dataDirSame: Selected directory is the same as current
defaultWorkspaceDirDesc: New terminals and chats start here when no project is selected. It lives under the data directory by default and rarely needs changing.
fontFamilyCjkHint: Include a CJK-capable monospace font (e.g. Maple Mono NF CN, Sarasa Mono SC, Microsoft YaHei) so Chinese text renders correctly; a CJK fallback is appended automatically when missing.
ccchanPetDescriptionHomie: Tiny smug patriotic cape-wearing superhero companion.
ccchanPetDescriptionDoro: A tiny white chibi pet with pink hair, purple eyes, and a side rose ribbon. Codex-pet standard atlas.
ccchanPetDescriptionYeShunguang: A school-themed companion inspired by Ye Shunguang from Zenless Zone Zero, carrying a notebook and pencil to accompany you while you work, wait, review, and sprint.
ccchanWanderHint: When off, cc-chan stays put and never moves on its own; you can still drag it.
ccchanSkinDirHint: Create <pet-id>/pet.json plus a spritesheet in this directory to add a custom pet; a pet with the same id as a built-in one overrides its appearance.
rendererHint: Auto prefers WebGL and falls back to DOM when the GPU, WebView, or glyph atlas is unreliable. Wallpaper transparency still requires DOM.
pathLinksEnabledHint: Show file and directory paths in terminal output as clickable links with open actions.
inlineImagesEnabledHint: Render images sent via OSC 1337 (iTerm inline image protocol) and SIXEL inside the terminal. Experimental and off by default: each terminal reserves up to 32 MB for cached images, and images are not restored after hibernation. Applies to newly opened terminal sessions.
autoTrustRegisteredProjectsHint: Skip Claude's folder trust prompt for projects and workspaces added to CC-Panes, including their git worktrees. Trust lets a repository's hooks and MCP settings run, so only register repositories you trust.
showContextUsageHint: Show the context usage indicator in the global and per-terminal status bars.
showStatusBarHint: Show a status bar below every terminal with its CLI, model, context usage, task queue, and project path. Turning it off gives the space back to the terminal.
taskQueueEnabledHint: Show a persistent task queue in every CLI status bar. Turning this off stops automatic dispatch and hides the controls without deleting queued tasks.
voiceDesc: Record from any terminal pane and insert the transcript into that pane without auto-submitting.
voiceShowFloatingButtonDesc: When off, the microphone button no longer appears in the terminal corner; the voice shortcut still works.
voiceEnableItn: Enable ITN for numbers, dates, and formatting
voiceLimitHint: This uses the Qwen-ASR OpenAI-compatible sync API for short recordings; the backend rejects audio over 10 MB.
voiceMimoHint: Xiaomi MiMo uses the open-platform audio understanding API. CC-Panes converts recordings to WAV locally and sends Base64 audio; use mimo-v2.5 or mimo-v2-omni.
voiceLocalHint: Runs sherpa-onnx on this computer. Audio never leaves the device and no API key is needed. The first time, download the engine and a model.
voiceLocalSenseVoiceDesc: Fast: a few seconds of speech transcribes in about a second. Chinese, Cantonese, English, Japanese and Korean, with punctuation. No dictionary support.
voiceLocalQwen3Desc: More accurate with fuller punctuation, and uses your dictionary. Larger, and takes a few seconds longer.
voiceLocalUnsupported: On-device transcription isn't available on this system.
voiceLocalSource: The engine and models come from the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx GitHub releases, are checked against SHA256, use your network proxy setting, and resume if interrupted.
voiceLocalReady: {{model}} is ready. Audio stays on this device.
voiceLocalNotReady: No on-device model yet. Use the button on the right to download one.
voiceDictionaryLocalUnsupported: SenseVoice doesn't support a dictionary. Switch to Qwen3-ASR or a cloud service to use it.
voiceCustomApiKey: API Key (leave empty for local servers)
voiceCustomPreferWav: Convert recording to WAV before sending
voiceCustomPreferWavDesc: Enable when the target service does not accept WebM, e.g. whisper.cpp server.
voiceCustomHint: Standard /v1/audio/transcriptions multipart endpoint, compatible with whisper.cpp server, faster-whisper, Groq, OpenAI, etc. Leave the API key empty for unauthenticated local servers. Language support depends on the target service.
voiceTranscribeWithDesc: The service that turns speech into text. Choose Off to disable voice input and hide the microphone buttons.
voiceTranscribeWithKeyMissing: No API key yet. Use the key button to set it up.
voiceLanguageDesc: Auto works for mixed speech; a fixed language is usually more accurate.
voiceTestDesc: Say a sentence and transcribe it with the current settings. The text only shows here.
voiceTestDesktopOnly: Transcription tests only run in the desktop app.
voiceMicrophoneDesc: Voice input uses the first connected microphone in this list. Drag or use the arrows to reorder.
voiceMicrophoneTestDesc: Record ten seconds and play it back. The audio stays on this device.
voicePlaybackFailed: Could not play this recording. Try recording again.
voiceMicDenied: Microphone access is blocked. Allow CC-Panes in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Microphone.
voiceMicEmpty: No audio was recorded. Try again.
voiceMicFailed: Could not open the microphone. Try again.
voiceDictionaryDesc: Names, project names and terms the service should spell your way.
voiceDictionaryTooLong: Each entry can be at most {{max}} characters.
voiceDictionaryFull: The dictionary holds at most {{max}} entries.
voiceMaxRecordSecondsDesc: Recording stops and transcribes automatically after this long (1–300 s).
shortcutsHint: Click a shortcut then press a new key combination to change it, press Esc to cancel
socksWarning: SOCKS5 proxy may not be supported by all tools (e.g. Claude Code, npm). HTTP proxy is recommended, or use a local proxy client to convert SOCKS5 to HTTP.
notifyOnlyUnfocused: Notify only when window is unfocused
providerDesc: Manage AI Provider configurations. After binding a Provider to a workspace, the corresponding environment variables will be injected when opening a terminal.
noProviders: No Providers yet, click the button below to add one
systemProviderDesc: Inject nothing — follow the current system config (e.g. cc-switch)
providerModelsHint: Configure the models available from this Provider and choose one launch default.
noProviderModels: No models configured; the CLI will continue using its native default
providerModelContextWindowInvalid: Context window must be a whole number from 1,000 to 10,000,000
providerModelIdsUnique: Model IDs must be unique within a Provider
appDescription: Multi-instance split-pane manager for Claude Code
updateBodyFallback: This release includes improvements and bug fixes.
updateRestartWarning: The app will close and restart. Any running tasks will be interrupted.
updateRestartBusyWarning: An agent is still running. Continuing will interrupt those tasks immediately.

featureTips.terminalPassthroughHint: While the terminal has focus this shortcut is passed to the terminal, so pressing it does nothing here. Click outside the terminal first (the tab bar or sidebar), then press it.

commandPalette.title: Jump anywhere with the Command Palette
commandPalette.body: Commands, workspaces, layouts - one input reaches them all. Hands on the keyboard, a few letters away.
commandPalette.bodyUnbound: Bind the Command Palette in Settings, then find commands, workspaces, and layouts quickly.

layoutSwitcher.title: Switch task layouts at any time
layoutSwitcher.body: One split layout per kind of task - switch without rearranging windows. Open the picker to swap the whole working surface.
layoutSwitcher.bodyUnbound: Bind the layout picker in Settings to move quickly between task views.

miniMode.title: Collapse into a mini terminal
miniMode.body: Watching long output doesn't need the whole workbench. Collapse into a lightweight terminal floating on the desktop; press again to return.
miniMode.bodyUnbound: Bind Mini Mode in Settings to collapse the window into a lightweight terminal.

launcher.title: Create tabs from one launcher
launcher.body: Project, CLI, runtime, launch options - one entry point covers them all. New tabs start here.
launcher.bodyUnbound: Bind New Tab in Settings to open the unified project, CLI, and runtime launcher.

interfaceShapes.title: Try interface shapes
interfaceShapes.body: Colors stay, only corners, dividers, and surface treatment change - six personalities per theme. Take a lap through theme settings.

dispatchOrchestration.title: Let one AI command a fleet of AIs
dispatchOrchestration.body: Say "run these in parallel" and this session splits the work, spawns several Claude / Codex workers, and each one reports back on its own when it finishes. You only start it and wrap it up. The orchestration panel shows every worker's live status.

worktreeIsolation.title: Work in parallel without touching your main tree
worktreeIsolation.body: A worktree checks out another branch into its own directory, so each dispatched worker edits its own copy while your main working tree stays clean. Right-click a project → "Worktree Manager" to create, remove, or open a terminal inside one.

aiPanel.title: Let the AI render a real panel for you
aiPanel.body: An AI in a terminal can only emit characters. Over MCP it can post a Markdown or HTML panel instead: comparison tables, progress boards, even buttons for you to decide with. Panels land in the right dock, and closing one keeps its content in history.

skills.title: Common workflows are already baked into the AI
skills.body: Common workflows ship as skills pre-installed into each CLI - plain words trigger them. For the list: type / in a session (Codex uses the ccpanes- prefix), or Settings > Tools > Skills.

rightDock.title: The right dock: watch while it runs
rightDock.body: What the AI changed, what Git saw - watch while it runs. The panel button at the far right of the title bar opens it; dock and sidebar can stay open together.

browserTab.title: The browser is the AI's hand, not yours
browserTab.body: A real browser can run in a split pane. The AI opens it over MCP: let it load your dev server, take a screenshot, click around, and run JavaScript to verify a change. Screenshots, clicks, and JS evaluation are supported on Windows and macOS (JS evaluation requires macOS 11 or later).

cleanupConfirmDescription: This removes CC-Panes global CLI files and hooks from registered projects. Workspaces, sessions, and other user configuration are preserved.

aboutGroups.checkUpdateDesc: Check manually whether a newer version is available.
aboutGroups.openLogDirDesc: Attach these log files when troubleshooting or reporting a bug.

mcpHubSummary: {{injected}} injected by the launch profile · {{layer}} in this layer

mcpEmptyFiltered: No MCP servers from this source
mcpLegacyFound: Found {{count}} server(s) in .claude/settings.local.json that are not imported yet (CC-Panes no longer writes that file)
providerTypeConfigDesc: Point to Claude Code config directory or ccswitch profile
providerTypeGrokDesc: Use xAI API key (XAI_API_KEY). Custom base URL must also be configured per-model in ~/.grok/config.toml
selectWorkspaceFirst: Please select a workspace in the sidebar first
pathNotExist: Path does not exist or cannot be read

defaultCliToolDesc: Default CLI tool for self-dialogue, session resume, and other scenarios
searchScopeDesc: Controls the range of file search indexing
searchScopeFullDiskHint: Full disk search requires more memory, initial indexing may take a few minutes
wallpaperDesc: Background wallpaper for the main pane area. Workspaces can override or disable it individually.
wallpaperImageHint: Imported files are copied into the app data directory
wallpaperOpacityHint: Strength of the wallpaper itself. Lowering it fades the wallpaper toward the background colour — set it to 100% to see the wallpaper clearly.
wallpaperTerminalOpacityHint: Strength of the terminal's own backdrop. Lowering it reveals more wallpaper; 0% puts the text straight on the wallpaper.
wallpaperGlassBlurHint: Frost applied by the panel sitting on top of the wallpaper — a separate layer from "Blur" above. Raising it washes out video; defaults to 0.
wallpaperMusicUseVideoAudioHint: Ignores the music file below; the video itself stays muted and the sound plays on a separate track
screenshotDesc: Capture a screen region and copy the file path to clipboard for Claude Code to reference.
screenshotSaved: Screenshot saved, path copied to clipboard
quickTerminalDesc: Toggle a drop-down (Quake-style) terminal from anywhere with a global hotkey. The window keeps its session, scrollback, and cursor between show/hide.
quickTerminalAutoHideHint: Collapse the window automatically when it loses focus
quickTerminalHeightHint: Share of screen height when shown (15% - 85%)
searchKeywords.quickTerminal: quick terminal, dropdown, quake, global shortcut, hotkey
cliLaunchersDesc: Set the local command used to start each CLI tool. Leave blank to use the default command and PATH detection. This only affects newly launched local sessions.
presetXaiDesc: Official xAI API key for Grok CLI
ccSwitchImportOk: Imported {{imported}} providers; skipped {{skipped}} duplicates, {{empty}} empty or unresolved configurations, and {{unsupported}} unsupported providers

ccSwitchImportNone: No importable providers found in cc-switch
selectPresetOrCustom: Select a preset or create a custom configuration
emptyDesc: Add a Provider to connect Claude Code, Codex and other AI tools
providerLaunchHint: This page only manages credentials. To start a session with one, press {{shortcut}} to open the launcher.
systemEnvNone: No Anthropic environment variables or cc-switch config detected
systemEnvRuntimeWarning: This probe inspects the local host process; it does not represent the target environment under {{runtime}}.
resumeIdBackfillHint: Legacy mechanism that guesses resume ids by scanning session directories. Superseded by deterministic binding (Claude issued id / Codex title capture). Keep off unless troubleshooting.
lowerSessionPriorityHint: Runs each session's process tree (the CLI and everything it spawns — cargo, rg, npm) at below-normal priority so a busy pane can't starve the UI. Idle cores are still used fully, so build throughput is unaffected. Applies to newly started sessions.
terminalDaemonHint: Host PTYs in a standalone daemon so desktop, Web and mobile attach to the same live sessions. Takes effect after app restart.
daemonOrphanTtlHint: Idle sessions with no viewer and no recent output are reclaimed oldest-first after this duration (default 24 hours). Applies within ~1 minute, no restart needed.
daemonOrphanReaperDisabledHint: When checked the daemon never auto-reclaims unwatched sessions (replaces the old "set expiry to 0" semantics).
orphanSessionReclaimedBody: Cleaned up {{count}} background terminal sessions with no panel reference.
disableWslUsageScanDesc: Stop scanning usage data inside WSL so the app never wakes the WSL VM (Vmmem memory usage)
showSystemResources: Show system resources in the status bar
allowMcpYoloProfiles: Allow agents to manage YOLO launch profiles
allowMcpYoloProfilesHint: Allow orchestration agents to create, bind, or explicitly launch profiles with --dangerously-skip-permissions. Agents can bypass permission prompts when enabled; turn this on only if you accept that risk.
followAgentLaunch: Follow agent launches to their layout
followAgentLaunchHint: When off (default), workers a leader launches are still created in the target layout, but the view stays where you are — a toast with a jump link is shown instead. Turn on to restore automatic switching.

orchestratorAlert.retrying: MCP service binding failed. Waiting for retry attempt {{attempt}}. Next retry: {{time}}
orchestratorAlert.attempting: MCP service is making bind attempt {{attempt}}.
orchestratorAlert.impact: Injected CLI sessions cannot use the MCP tools.

orchestratorAlert.escapeSuffix: to another fixed port and restart the app.

automations.title: Automations
automations.description: Run an agent prompt on a schedule. Sessions run headless with the ccpanes MCP injected; results land in the run history.
automations.name: Name
automations.autoApproveHint: Headless runs cannot answer permission prompts. When enabled, the first allow option is selected automatically.
automations.listEmpty: No tasks yet. Pick a template on the right to start.
automations.heroDescription: Let an agent handle recurring work on a schedule, so you don't have to do it by hand.
automations.runsEmptyHint: Runs will show up here once it fires. Use "Run now" to try it first.
automations.promptPlaceholder: Describe what the agent should do on every run. Be specific.

standup.title: Daily standup summary
standup.description: Weekday mornings: yesterday's commits, unmerged branches and open work.
standup.prompt: Summarize this repository's git commits from the last 24 hours (author, key points), list unmerged local branches and uncommitted changes in the working tree, and finish with the 3 most important things to do today. Output concise Markdown.

testPatrol.title: Test patrol
testPatrol.description: Run the tests daily and explain any failures with likely fixes.
testPatrol.prompt: Run this project's test suite. If everything passes, reply with one line and the duration. For each failure, give the error summary, the most likely cause and the suggested fix location (file:line). Do not modify code.

dependencyAudit.title: Dependency audit
dependencyAudit.description: Every Monday, check dependencies for known vulnerabilities and stale versions.
dependencyAudit.prompt: Audit this project's dependencies: run the applicable audit commands (npm audit, cargo audit, pip-audit, ...), list packages with known vulnerabilities, their severity and the safe version to upgrade to, then list dependencies more than one major version behind. Do not modify lock files.

weeklyReport.title: Weekly report draft
weeklyReport.description: Friday evening: draft a weekly report from this week's commits.
weeklyReport.prompt: Based on this repository's git commits since Monday, draft a weekly report grouped into features, fixes and refactors with key points for each, and end with suggestions for next week. Use Markdown.

todoSweep.title: TODO sweep
todoSweep.description: Weekly scan of TODO / FIXME comments, sorted by urgency.
todoSweep.prompt: Scan the repository for TODO, FIXME and HACK comments, group them by file, flag the ones that look most urgent or stale, and output a table (location, text, suggested action). Do not modify code.

branchCleanup.title: Branch cleanup
branchCleanup.description: Fridays: list merged or stale branches for you to confirm deleting.
branchCleanup.prompt: List local and remote branches in this repository that are merged into the main branch or have had no commits for 30+ days, with last commit date and author. Only give the list and recommendations; do not delete anything.

docsDrift.title: Docs drift check
docsDrift.description: Weekly check that the docs still match the code.
docsDrift.prompt: Compare the README and docs/ with the current code. Find outdated commands, config keys, file paths or API descriptions and list each with its location and a suggested edit. Do not edit files directly.

logTriage.title: Error log triage
logTriage.description: Every morning, group recent errors and spot new ones.
logTriage.prompt: Review this project's error logs from the last 24 hours (find them per the project's conventions), group and count errors by type, flag errors that are new today, and name the one most worth fixing first and why.

quickCommands.title: Quick Commands
quickCommands.description: Save terminal commands and agent prompts, then run them from the Command Palette or a tab menu.
quickCommands.dialogDescription: Configure the command content, storage scope, and run target.
quickCommands.projectScopeUnavailable: Activate a project to save project-scoped commands.
quickCommands.emptyDescription: Add a command to run it from the Command Palette or a tab context menu.

quickCommands.noCliTool: The agent prompt has no CLI tool configured

wechatComponent.targetInvalid: Enter an SSH host (no spaces, can't start with -)

feishuCli.skillsHint: Skills go into the resource library; toggle them per launch profile on the Skills page.
feishuCli.waitingBrowser: The authorization page is open in your browser; this updates when you finish

skillLibrary.intro: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md that an agent loads when it needs it. The library keeps each one once; turn it on for the launch profiles that need it. CC-Panes injects it when a session starts and never changes ~/.claude or similar folders.
skillLibrary.emptyTitle: No skills in the library yet
skillLibrary.emptyHint: Paste a source above to install, or bring in ones your agents already have (below).

tagHint.gone: Its source no longer has this skill. It stays here until you remove it.
tagHint.update: Changed upstream since it was installed.
tagHint.unchecked: Couldn't check for updates this time.
tagHint.edited: You changed it here since it was fetched. Updating asks before it replaces your changes.
tagHint.folderMissing: The linked folder is gone; sessions won't load it.

skillLibrary.keptEdited: Kept as you changed them: {{names}}. Update each from its row to replace your changes.
skillLibrary.checkAllCurrent: Every skill is up to date
skillLibrary.removeConfirm: Remove the skill “{{name}}”? It is turned off for every launch profile and its folder is moved to the backups.
skillLibrary.removeConfirmFolder: Remove the skill “{{name}}”? It is turned off for every launch profile; the folder it links to stays where it is.
skillLibrary.backupHint: Their folders are moved to CC-Panes' backups (backups/skills in the data folder), not deleted.

confirmUpdate.title: Replace your changes to {{name}} with the upstream version?
confirmUpdate.body: You changed {{name}} here since it was fetched. Updating puts the upstream version in its place; yours is moved to the backups.
confirmUpdate.unknownBody: {{name}} was installed before CC-Panes tracked changes, so it can't tell whether you edited it. Updating puts the upstream version in its place; the current one is moved to the backups.

confirmGone.title: Remove {{count}} skills removed upstream?
confirmGone.body: Their sources no longer have these skills. Removing them also turns them off for every launch profile.

scope.mcpGlobalDesc: Applies to all workspaces. Workspace-level MCP servers are layered on top.

scope.credentialsDesc: Provider credentials are shared globally and referenced by launch profiles.

terminalColorHint: Leave empty to follow the theme. Low contrast colors are adjusted for visible marks and readable text. Try the DOM renderer if the cursor or selection is still missing.
autoCloseCompletedTasks: Allow completed tasks to close automatically
autoCloseCompletedTasksHint: Off by default. Opt in separately from each task menu. Tabs close after the task completes, the process exits, and a result summary is saved, with a 30-second grace period. Results remain in task details.
mcpArgsHelp: Separate arguments with spaces. Quote values containing spaces; use "" for an empty argument. Single quotes preserve Windows backslashes. Inside double quotes, escape quotes and backslashes with a backslash. Variables and commands are never expanded.
imInboundEnabled: Receive messages and let a bot reply
imInboundHint: Messages you send to this Telegram bot go to a bot in Contacts on the desktop, and the reply comes back. Only messages in the numeric Chat ID above, from the allowed users below, are accepted; send /help for commands.
imInboundConfirm: Allowed senders will be able to make the bot read and write files and run commands on this computer (within the bot's auto-approve setting). By default only you, in a private chat, are accepted; if the Chat ID is a group, only the users you list under Allowed user IDs are. Turn this on?
imInboundAllowedUsersHint: Numeric Telegram user IDs, comma-separated. Leave empty to accept only yourself in a private chat (the Chat ID is your user ID); group chats must list users here.
imInboundNeedsNumericChatId: Receiving messages needs a numeric Chat ID (such as 123456789 or -100…). @usernames can be taken over after a rename and are not accepted.
islandDesc: A session status capsule at the top of the screen: what is running, who needs you, quota left.

browserImport.title: Browser
browserImport.description: Sign-in state and data for the built-in browser.
browserImport.keywords: browser built-in Chrome import login sign in cookie cookies session Brave Edge Arc keychain
browserImport.importTitle: Import sign-in state from another browser
browserImport.importHint: Copies the cookies of one profile in Chrome or a similar browser into the built-in browser once. Afterwards the two stay independent.
browserImport.noSources: No importable browser found (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Arc and Chromium are supported).
browserImport.noteQuit: Quit {{browser}} completely first, otherwise recent sign-ins may not be on disk yet.
browserImport.noteKeychain: macOS will ask for keychain access. Choose Allow so the cookies can be decrypted.
browserImport.noteOneTime: This is a one-time copy. Signing in or out on either side later is not synced.
browserImport.noteRelogin: Some sites check the device or bind the session, so you may still need to sign in again.
browserImport.resultFailed: {{failed}} more could not be decrypted and were skipped.

errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM: Importing is not supported on this platform yet. Only macOS is supported (on Windows, Chromium browsers use app-bound encryption that cannot be read).
errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND: That browser or profile was not found. Make sure it is installed and has been opened at least once.
errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_KEYCHAIN_DENIED: Keychain access was denied, so the cookies cannot be decrypted. Choose Allow in the system prompt when you retry.
errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_KEYCHAIN_NOT_FOUND: The browser's encryption key (Safe Storage) was not found in the keychain.
errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_READ_FAILED: Could not read the browser's cookie database. Quit that browser and try again.
errors.BROWSER_IMPORT_NO_WEBVIEW: The built-in browser is not ready yet. Try again in a moment.
